verses.english: Linked Discourses 12.46
5. Householders
A Certain Brahmin
At Sāvatthī.

verses.pali: Atha kho aññataro brāhmaṇo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṁ sammodi.
verses.english: Then a certain brahmin went up to the Buddha, and exchanged greetings with him.

verses.pali: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho so brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to the Buddha:

verses.pali: “Kiṁ nu kho, bho gotama, so karoti so paṭisaṁvedayatī”ti?
verses.english: “Worthy Gotama, are he who does the deed and he who experiences the result one and the same?”

verses.pali: “‘So karoti so paṭisaṁvedayatī’ti kho, brāhmaṇa, ayameko anto”.
verses.english: “‘He who does the deed and he who experiences the result are one and the same’: this is one extreme, brahmin.”

verses.pali: “Kiṁ pana, bho gotama, añño karoti, añño paṭisaṁvedayatī”ti?
verses.english: “Then is he who does the deed one and he who experiences the result another?”

verses.pali: “‘Añño karoti, añño paṭisaṁvedayatī’ti kho, brāhmaṇa, ayaṁ dutiyo anto.
verses.english: “‘He who does the deed is one and he who experiences the result is another’: this is the second extreme.

verses.pali: Ete te, brāhmaṇa, ubho ante anupagamma majjhena tathāgato dhammaṁ deseti:
verses.english: Avoiding these two extremes, the Realized One teaches by the middle way:
‘Ignorance is a requirement for choices.
Choices are a requirement for consciousness. …
That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.
When ignorance fades away and ceases with nothing left over, choices cease.
When choices cease …
That is how this entire mass of suffering ceases.’”

verses.pali: Evaṁ vutte, so brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: When he said this, the brahmin said to the Buddha,
“Excellent, worthy Gotama! Excellent! …

verses.pali: upāsakaṁ maṁ bhavaṁ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṁ saraṇaṁ gatan”ti.
verses.english: From this day forth, may the worthy Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”
